CVE-2020-10650 is a jackson-databind deserialization gadget issue that requires both (a) the specific gadget classes (org.apache.ignite.cache.jta.jndi.CacheJndiTmLookup, org.apache.ignite.cache.jta.jndi.CacheJndiTmFactory, or org.quartz.utils.JNDIConnectionProvider) on the classpath, and (b) polymorphic type handling (enableDefaultTyping/PolymorphicTypeValidator-gated typing) enabled on a mapper processing untrusted input. Neither condition exists in PingFederate: no Ignite or Quartz libraries are present in the PingFederate image, and PingFederate does not enable polymorphic deserialization on any mapper that processes external input.

The Netty vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-33870 and CVE-2026-33871) are present in PingFederate through both direct library inclusion (netty-codec-http.jar, netty-codec-http2.jar) and transitive dependencies (e.g., aws-kms-master-key-encryptor.jar via the AWS SDK). However, PingFederate does not use Netty as its HTTP server or request-processing engine. All inbound HTTP and HTTP/2 traffic is handled by Jetty. Netty is only used for internal or outbound communication (e.g., AWS SDK clients, Redis integrations) and is not exposed to external clients. Both vulnerabilities require attacker-controlled HTTP/1.1 or HTTP/2 traffic to be parsed directly by Netty in a server or proxy role. Since Netty is not used in this capacity within PingFederate, these vulnerabilities are not exploitable through PingFederate’s external interfaces. Therefore, this is assessed as a dependency-level vulnerability with no direct exploitability in the PingFederate runtime architecture. Remediation will be addressed through dependency upgrades in a future release.

This vulnerability in Apache MINA involves unsafe deserialization of data via the IoBuffer.getObject() method, which can allow remote code execution if an application processes untrusted serialized input. PingFederate includes Apache MINA version that is within the affected range; however, PingFederate does not use the deserialization functionality associated with this issue (including IoBuffer.getObject() or related serialization codecs). As a result, there is no exploitable attack path in PingFederate. As a best practice and for defense-in-depth, Ping Identity plans to update the MINA dependency to a patched version.

This vulnerability in Apache MINA relates to improper validation during class resolution in deserialization, which could allow unauthorized classes to be instantiated and potentially lead to remote code execution if untrusted serialized data is processed. PingFederate includes Apache MINA version that is within the affected range; however, PingFederate does not invoke any of the deserialization APIs involved in this issue and does not process untrusted serialized input through MINA. Therefore, the vulnerable code path is not reachable, and there is no impact to PingFederate. The MINA dependency will be upgraded in a future release as a precaution.

This vulnerability in Apache MINA allows a bypass of deserialization protections where static initializers may be executed before proper class validation, potentially enabling remote code execution when deserializing untrusted data. Because PingFederate does not deserialize untrusted data using MINA, there is no exploitable condition. No confidentiality or integrity impact has been identified; the issue is limited to potential denial of service.

PingFederate's CORS enforcement is implemented as plain servlet Filters — CrossOriginFilter.java:68 (public class CrossOriginFilter implements Filter, a ported copy of Jetty's older CORS filter, per its copyright header) and the equivalent AdminApiCrossOriginFilter in the admin-api module. Neither has any code relationship to Netty's io.netty.handler.codec.http.cors.CorsHandler — different class hierarchy, different origin-evaluation logic entirely. The specific logical-operator bug described in this CVE lives inside Netty's CorsHandler, which PingFederate's servlet filters never call.

Even setting the version aside, brace-expansion does not appear in either package.json's dependencies block — it's reachable only transitively via devDependencies (minimatch@3.1.2 → brace-expansion, itself pulled in by the webpack/eslint/jest build-tooling chain). Not vulnerable. CVE-2026-41001 is specific to Spring Boot's ArtemisEmbeddedConfigurationFactory, which sets up an embedded Artemis message broker. PingFederate doesn't use: Spring Boot - no spring-boot dependency found in any pom.xml or the dependency dumps in the repo. PingFederate doesn't use: Artemis/ActiveMQ - zero references anywhere in the codebase. There's no embedded message broker in this codebase for the predictable-directory/symlink attack to target, so the code path the CVE describes doesn't exist here.

PingFederate embeds Eclipse Jetty as its servlet container, so exposure to CVE-2026-10051 tracks the bundled Jetty version exactly — there's no PingFederate-specific code that touches HTTP trailers or Jetty's connection-recycling internals, so PF neither introduces nor mitigates this bug independently. PF 13.0 will be updated with a non-vulnerable version of jetty.

PingFederate is not vulnerable to CVE-2026-56816. The vulnerable class (Http3FrameCodec, in the netty-codec-http3 artifact) is not present in the product at all. The attack surface doesn't exist either. The CVE requires an attacker to open QUIC streams against a Netty-based HTTP/3 server. PingFederate's HTTP listener is Jetty, not Netty - its Netty usage is purely client-side (Redis via Lettuce, AWS services). Even if the http3 codec jar were on the classpath, nothing would instantiate Http3FrameCodec in a server role.
PingFederate is not vulnerable to CVE-2026-56820. The vulnerable component (io.netty:netty-handler-ssl-ocsp) is not present in the product, and no code path invokes Netty's OCSP validation.

Repsonse varies for each PF version. Most PF versions use a non-vulnerable jetty version. PF 13.0 is still awaiting an upgrade. Two mitigating points: Jetty itself refuses to serve aliased/unresolved resources, so static-file disclosure is not the issue - the risk is only to application code that makes authorization decisions on the unresolved path. PingFederate's own routing/authz code uses exact equals() matches on getServletPath() and strips path parameters explicitly, so a /foo;/../bar confusion fails closed rather than bypassing anything. So practical exploitability is low.

PingFederate is not meaningfully exposed to CVE-2026-6790. The underlying issue is that Jetty, on earlier versions across HTTP/1, HTTP/2, and HTTP/3, did not strictly enforce that the request authority matches the Host header, which the newer HTTP RFCs (9110/9112) now require. In PingFederate's runtime engine, however, the URLs used in redirects, endpoint metadata, and other security-relevant output are constructed from the administrator-configured base URL, and the request's hostname is only substituted in when it matches a configured virtual-host whitelist or a configured OAuth issuer. This means an attacker-supplied authority that isn't part of that configuration is simply disregarded rather than reflected back into any URL. We've also identified a small number of secondary locations that construct URLs more directly from the incoming request, and we're proactively hardening those as an additional defense-in-depth measure, along with planning an upgrade to a patched Jetty version in an upcoming release.

PingFederate codebase is not vulnerable to CVE-2026-10050. The vulnerable component isn't used. No references to DigestAuthenticator or Jetty's digest auth constants anywhere in Java code. No <auth-method>DIGEST</auth-method> (or any auth-method) declarations in any web.xml. No Jetty LoginService/SecurityHandler-based container authentication in use at all — PingFederate implements its own authentication layers (admin console auth, OAuth client auth, etc.) rather than delegating to Jetty's container security.

PingFederate is not exploitable for CVE-2026-59903. The bug is in Netty's server-side CorsHandler, but PF serves HTTP with Jetty and handles CORS in its own servlet filters - no PF code imports io.netty at all, and netty exists only as unused client-side transport (AWS SDK, lettuce — which doesn't even ship the affected netty-codec-http module).

PingFederate adopted HttpClient5 in version 13.0.0. It uses the classic blocking client exclusively, and leaves content decompression enabled, so the leaky code path is live. The realistic impact is DoS-only: an attacker who gets PF to fetch an endpoint they control (e.g., a jwks_uri or CIMD metadata URL) can return bogus Content-Encoding headers to leak pooled connections until outbound OIDC/SOAP/datastore calls - and the SSO flows depending on them — start failing. Even on affected versions, the defect is a connection-pool resource leak (CWE-772) triggerable only by malformed responses from servers PingFederate connects to as an HTTP client; the impact is limited to availability of outbound connections (CVSS 3.1: 5.3 Medium, A:L — no confidentiality or integrity impact).
PingFederate doesn't ship netty-codec-haproxy in any form — it's absent from the dependency graph, the scan inventory, and the shaded jars — so CVE-2026-55851 doesn't apply.

Not Vulnerable. This CVE affects the XmlFrameDecoder class in the optional netty-codec-xml module, which PingFederate does not ship or use. PingFederate includes Netty only as a transitive dependency of the Lettuce Redis client and the AWS SDK, which use Netty's core transport, buffer, and HTTP codec modules — the XML codec module containing the vulnerable code path is not present in any PingFederate release. Because the affected class is not on the classpath and no PingFederate feature performs XML frame decoding over Netty, the trickle-fed </ CPU-exhaustion attack described in this CVE is not exploitable against PingFederate.

Not Vulnerable. This CVE affects the XmlDecoder class in Netty's optional netty-codec-xml module, which PingFederate does not include in any release. PingFederate carries Netty only as a transitive dependency of the Lettuce Redis client and the AWS SDK, which use Netty's core transport and HTTP modules; neither the XML codec module nor the Aalto XML parser it depends on is present on the PingFederate classpath. Because the vulnerable class cannot be loaded and no PingFederate component performs XML decoding through Netty, the DOCTYPE/external-entity processing risk described in this CVE does not apply to PingFederate.

This CVE affects Jinja, a templating engine for the Python programming language, in applications that render untrusted Jinja templates. PingFederate is a Java-based product and does not ship, bundle, or execute Jinja or any Python runtime component; a search of the PingFederate codebase confirms no usage of this library. As the affected software is not present in the product, this vulnerability does not apply to PingFederate.

Not Vulnerable. This CVE affects SctpMessageCompletionHandler in Netty's optional SCTP modules, which PingFederate does not ship. PingFederate includes Netty only as a transitive dependency of the Lettuce Redis client and the AWS SDK, which use Netty's core TCP transport, buffer, and HTTP codec modules — the SCTP transport and codec modules containing the vulnerable code are not present in any PingFederate release, and PingFederate does not accept or process SCTP traffic on any listener. Because the affected class is not on the classpath and no SCTP endpoint exists, the memory-exhaustion attack described in this CVE is not exploitable against PingFederate.

Not Vulnerable. This CVE affects HAProxyMessageEncoder in Netty's optional netty-codec-haproxy module, which PingFederate does not ship in any release. PingFederate includes Netty only as a transitive dependency of the Lettuce Redis client and the AWS SDK, which rely on Netty's core transport and HTTP modules; the HAProxy codec module containing the vulnerable encoder is not present on the classpath. Additionally, the vulnerability requires an application that actively emits HAProxy PROXY-protocol headers with attacker-controlled AF_UNIX socket addresses — a function PingFederate does not perform — so this issue is not exploitable against PingFederate.

Not Vulnerable. This CVE affects StompSubframeEncoder in Netty's optional netty-codec-stomp module, which PingFederate does not include in any release. PingFederate carries Netty only as a transitive dependency of the Lettuce Redis client and the AWS SDK, which use Netty's core transport and HTTP modules; the STOMP codec module containing the vulnerable encoder is not present on the classpath. Furthermore, PingFederate does not implement or communicate over the STOMP messaging protocol in any capacity, so the header-injection scenario described in this CVE cannot occur in the product.

Affected version present - low exploitability. PingFederate ships the affected netty-codec-dns module as a transitive dependency of the Lettuce Redis client, so the vulnerable code is present on the classpath. However, this code path is only exercised when PingFederate is configured to use Redis for session/state storage, and exploitation requires an attacker who can return malformed DNS responses to PingFederate's resolver - meaning control of, or an on-path position relative to, the deployment's DNS infrastructure; the impact is limited to gradual memory exhaustion (denial of service), with no confidentiality or integrity effect. Ping Identity is addressing this by upgrading the bundled Netty libraries to a fixed version (4.2.16.Final or later) in an upcoming release; deployments not using Redis, or using trusted internal DNS, are not exposed in the interim.

Not Vulnerable. This CVE affects the HAProxyMessageDecoder in Netty's optional netty-codec-haproxy module, which PingFederate does not ship in any release. PingFederate includes Netty only as a transitive dependency of the Lettuce Redis client and the AWS SDK, neither of which pulls in the HAProxy codec module, and PingFederate does not terminate the PROXY protocol through Netty. Because the vulnerable decoder is not on the classpath, this issue is not exploitable against PingFederate.

Not Vulnerable. This CVE affects Netty's QUIC codec (QuicheQuicServerCodec), an optional module that PingFederate does not include in any release. PingFederate does not implement QUIC or HTTP/3 on any listener; all PingFederate endpoints are served over TCP/TLS by the embedded Jetty container, and Netty is present only as a transitive dependency of the Lettuce Redis client and AWS SDK, which do not use the QUIC codec. As the vulnerable code is not present and no QUIC server exists in the product, the address-validation/amplification issue described in this CVE does not apply.

Affected version present - low exploitability. PingFederate ships the affected netty-resolver-dns module as a transitive dependency of the Lettuce Redis client, so the vulnerable code is present on the classpath. This resolver is only exercised when PingFederate is configured to use Redis for session/state storage, it resolves only the administrator-configured Redis endpoint hostnames, and exploitation requires an attacker able to supply crafted DNS responses to PingFederate's resolver - i.e., control of or an on-path position within the deployment's DNS infrastructure. Ping Identity is addressing this by upgrading the bundled Netty libraries to a fixed version in an upcoming release; deployments not using Redis, or using trusted internal DNS, are not exposed in the interim.

Not Vulnerable. This CVE affects Netty's optional netty-transport-sctp module, which PingFederate does not ship in any release. PingFederate includes Netty only via the Lettuce Redis client and AWS SDK, which use Netty's core TCP transport modules, and PingFederate does not accept or process SCTP traffic on any listener. Because the affected handler is not on the classpath and no SCTP endpoint exists, this memory-exhaustion issue is not exploitable against PingFederate.

Affected version present - low exploitability. PingFederate ships the affected netty-resolver-dns module as a transitive dependency of the Lettuce Redis client, so the vulnerable code is present on the classpath. The resolver runs only when PingFederate is configured for Redis session/state storage and resolves only the fixed, administrator-configured Redis hostnames — an attacker cannot cause PingFederate to query an attacker-controlled authoritative name server, so poisoning requires prior control of, or an on-path position within, the deployment's own DNS infrastructure. Ping Identity is addressing this by upgrading the bundled Netty libraries to a fixed version in an upcoming release; deployments not using Redis, or using trusted internal DNS, are not exposed in the interim.

Not Vulnerable. This CVE affects RedisArrayAggregator in Netty's optional netty-codec-redis module, which PingFederate does not ship in any release. Although PingFederate does support Redis for session/state storage, it communicates with Redis through the Lettuce client, which implements its own RESP protocol codec and does not use Netty's Redis codec module. Because the vulnerable handler is not on the classpath, this memory-leak issue is not exploitable against PingFederate.

Affected version present - low exploitability. PingFederate ships the affected netty-codec-http2 module as a transitive dependency of the AWS SDK's Netty HTTP client, so the vulnerable code is present on the classpath. However, this code path runs only as an HTTP/2 client within optional AWS integrations (such as the DynamoDB provisioning data store), where the remote peer is an AWS service endpoint reached over TLS with full certificate validation - exploitation would require a malicious or fully compromised AWS endpoint, and the impact is limited to memory exhaustion (denial of service). PingFederate's own inbound HTTP listeners are served by Jetty, not Netty, and are unaffected; Ping Identity is addressing this by upgrading the bundled Netty libraries to a fixed version in an upcoming release.

Not Vulnerable. This CVE affects the HAProxy PROXY protocol v2 codec in Netty's optional netty-codec-haproxy module, which PingFederate does not ship in any release. PingFederate does not parse the PROXY protocol through Netty, and the module is not pulled in by the Lettuce Redis client or AWS SDK dependencies that account for Netty's presence in the product. Because the vulnerable codec is not on the classpath, this issue is not exploitable against PingFederate.

Not Vulnerable. This CVE affects Netty's optional HTTP/3 codec, which PingFederate does not include in any release. PingFederate does not implement HTTP/3 or QUIC on any interface; all product endpoints are served over TCP/TLS by the embedded Jetty container, and the Netty libraries present in the product (via the Lettuce Redis client and AWS SDK) do not include or use the HTTP/3 codec. As the vulnerable code is not present and no HTTP/3 service exists, this issue does not apply to PingFederate.

Not Vulnerable (vulnerable configuration not used). The affected code resides in Netty's netty-handler module, which PingFederate does ship, but the vulnerability only manifests when an application supplies a plain X509TrustManager instance directly to Netty's SslContextBuilder. PingFederate's only Netty TLS client usage is the Lettuce Redis integration, which is configured with a truststore file through a standard TrustManagerFactory — the platform trust managers this produces are full X509ExtendedTrustManager implementations that are never routed through the flawed wrapper, so hostname verification behaves as configured. Because the vulnerable API pattern is not used anywhere in the product, PingFederate is not exposed; the Netty upgrade planned for an upcoming release will remove the flawed code entirely.

Not Vulnerable. This CVE affects RedisArrayAggregator in Netty's optional netty-codec-redis module, which PingFederate does not ship in any release. PingFederate's Redis support uses the Lettuce client, which implements its own RESP protocol parsing and does not rely on Netty's Redis codec. Because the vulnerable class is not on the classpath, this memory-exhaustion issue is not exploitable against PingFederate.

Not Vulnerable. This CVE affects RedisArrayAggregator in Netty's optional netty-codec-redis module, which PingFederate does not ship in any release. While PingFederate supports Redis for session/state storage, it communicates with Redis exclusively through the Lettuce client, which implements its own RESP protocol codec and does not use Netty's Redis codec module. Because the vulnerable handler is not on the classpath, the buffer-pinning attack described in this CVE is not exploitable against PingFederate.

Not Vulnerable. While PingFederate ships the netty-handler library in an affected version range, this vulnerability requires three conditions that are all absent in PingFederate: the application must use Netty's OpenSSL TLS provider (PingFederate does not ship the required netty-tcnative library, so Netty operates exclusively on the standard JDK TLS provider), the application must supply a plain non-extended X509TrustManager (PingFederate's only Netty TLS usage — the Lettuce Redis client — is configured with a truststore through a standard TrustManagerFactory), and the JVM must be Java 25 or later (PingFederate runs on Java 17/21). Because none of the required preconditions exist in the product, the hostname-verification bypass described in this CVE is not exploitable against PingFederate; the planned Netty upgrade will nonetheless move the library out of the affected range.

Not Vulnerable. This CVE affects the jsoup HTML/XML parsing library, which PingFederate does not ship, bundle, or depend on in any release — a review of the product's complete dependency inventory and shipped libraries confirms jsoup is not present. PingFederate's XML processing is performed by hardened Xerces/XMLBeans and JAXP parsers with entity-expansion limits, not jsoup. As the affected software is not present in the product, this vulnerability does not apply to PingFederate.

PingFederate uses vulnerable jackson-databind, which is affected by CVE-2026-77310. The vulnerable code path is reachable through stored session deserialization, but exploitation requires write access to session storage backends (JDBC, LDAP, or Redis). The library will be upgraded in a future release of PingFederate.

PingFederate ships the OpenTelemetry java agent but does not attach it to the JVM unless distributed tracing is explicitly enabled (`pf.enable.distributed.tracing=true`; default false), so the vulnerable JDBC instrumentation is inactive out of the box. Additionally, the flaw requires database passwords to be embedded double-quoted in SQL CONNECT statement text; PingFederate authenticates to JDBC data stores via connection properties and never inlines credentials in SQL. Not exploitable in a standard deployment. Fixed in PingFederate 13.1, which ships OpenTelemetry 2.28.1 (at the 2.28.0 fix level).

PingFederate is NOT affected by CVE-2026-55153. The mchange-commons-java library in which the vulnerability resides is not bundled with, referenced by, or distributed as part of PingFederate in any supported release a a review of the product's dependency manifests and bundled libraries across releases 12.3 through 13.2 confirms the component is absent, including via the transitive paths through which it most commonly arrives (the c3p0 connection pool and Hibernate ORM). PingFederate performs JDBC connection pooling using Apache Commons DBCP, a separate implementation that does not share the affected code. Because the exploit path requires mchange-commons-java to be present on the server's classpath, the vulnerability is not exploitable in PingFederate, and no upgrade, mitigation, or configuration change is required; customers who see this CVE flagged in a scan of their environment should verify whether the detection originates from another application or shared library on the same host rather than from PingFederate itse

The Spring Framework versions bundled by PingFederate fall within the affected ranges - 12.3 ships Spring 5.3.39 and the latest release ships 6.2.19 - so scanner findings against these jars are expected. The vulnerability affects Spring MVC applications using the functional web framework with Server-Sent Events, and PingFederate does not use Spring MVC at all: it ships no spring-webmvc or WebFlux artifacts, and the Spring jars it does bundle (spring-core, spring-jdbc, spring-context, spring-web, etc.) are used solely for internal dependency injection, JDBC templating in the provisioner, and servlet context bootstrap - none of PingFederate's HTTP endpoints are served by Spring, and no SSE or reactive-stream APIs are used anywhere in the product. All PingFederate HTTP endpoints are served by Jetty and Jersey, so the vulnerable stream-handling code path is not reachable. PingFederate will update the bundled Spring Framework in an upcoming maintenance release to address the scanner finding; the issue itself is not exploitable in PingFederate.

PingFederate 12.3 bundles netty-codec-http 4.1.118.Final through the AWS SDK, which falls within the affected version range, so scanner findings against the bundled jar are expected. The vulnerable logic pairs requests and responses inside Netty's HTTP server codec, and PingFederate operates no Netty-based HTTP server: all PingFederate HTTP endpoints are served by Jetty, and the bundled Netty stack exists only as a client-side transport for the AWS SDK that PingFederate does not select (the AWS SDK is explicitly configured to use the Apache HTTP client instead). The attack requires a malicious client connecting to a Netty HTTP server that uses the affected codec, which does not exist in any PingFederate network-facing component, so the issue is not exploitable. PingFederate will include an upgrade to the fixed Netty version (4.1.137.Final) in an upcoming maintenance release to remediate the bundled copy; the latest release does not bundle netty-codec-http at all - the AWS SDK netty transport is excluded from the distribution, and the bundled Lettuce Redis client pulls only Netty core, DNS, and transport artifacts without the HTTP codec.

PingFederate 12.3 is not affected: it ships jackson-core 2.12.7, and the vulnerable NumberInput.looksLikeValidNumber() method does not exist in jackson-core releases prior to 2.17.0, which we verified against the shipped artifact. The latest PingFederate release ships jackson-core 2.21.1, which does contain the affected method and regular expressions, so that release is affected; the method is reachable through jackson-databind's default string-to-number coercion when deserializing JSON into numeric target types. PingFederate will remediate in an upcoming release by upgrading to the jackson-core version containing the fix, which replaces the backtracking regular expressions with a single-pass scan. Exposure on affected builds is mitigated by the fact that the reachable deserialization points are administrative interfaces requiring authenticated access.

PingFederate is not affected in 12.3 or the latest release. The vulnerability requires a parser created via JsonFactory.createParser(DataInput); PingFederate's JSON handling creates parsers only from InputStream and String sources, and we found no DataInput-based parser creation anywhere in the codebase. While the UTF8DataInputJsonParser class is present in the bundled jackson-core, the unreachable creation path means the accumulation behavior cannot be triggered by malformed request content. No upgrade is required for this issue specifically.

The affected caching behavior is present in the jackson-databind versions shipped by both 12.3 (2.12.7.1) and the latest release (2.21.1), which we confirmed at the bytecode level: fallback resolutions for unrecognized type IDs are cached without bound. Exploitation requires an endpoint that deserializes attacker-influenced type IDs into a polymorphic model with a fallback (defaultImpl) - in PingFederate these are Admin API configuration models (e.g., connection attribute sources), which require administrative privileges, and unknown type IDs are rejected by downstream validation even though the cache entry is created first. PingFederate will address this in an upcoming release by upgrading to the fixed jackson-databind version, which stops caching fallback resolutions and bounds the cache and cacheable ID length. The administrative authentication requirement substantially limits practical exposure in the meantime.

PingFederate is not affected in 12.3 or the latest release. The quadratic scan only executes when deserializing identity-enabled (@JsonIdentityInfo) collections or maps containing unresolved forward object references, and the PingFederate codebase contains no @JsonIdentityInfo usage or other object-identity deserialization configuration in any release. The affected path is therefore unreachable from any PingFederate deserialization entry point, and no upgrade is required for this issue.

Exposure to CVE-2025-68161 in PingFederate is conditional on customer configuration, and the underlying library has already been updated in recent releases. The vulnerability resides in the TLS transport of log4j-core's Socket Appender, which does not perform hostname verification of the log receiver's certificate; PingFederate ships log4j-core and provides Socket Appender definitions in its logging configuration that customers can enable and extend, so deployments that use a TLS Socket Appender for log shipping fall within the affected use case. Recent PingFederate releases ship log4j-core 2.25.4, which incorporates the fix (addressed upstream in 2.25.3); customers on older maintenance releases who use a TLS Socket Appender should update to a release containing the fixed library, or alternatively restrict the appender's trust store as described in the advisory. Deployments that do not use a TLS Socket Appender are not exposed, and no action is required in that case.

Not applicable. CVE-2026-8940 is a cross-site request forgery flaw in "WP Meta Sort Posts", a third-party WordPress plugin, and PingFederate contains no WordPress component, PHP code, or any software from this vendor; the finding has no relationship to PingFederate and appears to be a scanning error or a misattributed component in the customer's environment. No action is required.

PingFederate is not affected by CVE-2026-93561. The netty-codec-memcache module is not bundled with PingFederate in any supported release (12.3 through 13.2), and PingFederate does not speak the memcache protocol, so the vulnerable code path - parsing binary responses from a memcache server - does not exist in the product. No upgrade, mitigation, or configuration change is required.

PingFederate is not affected by CVE-2026-93566. PingFederate's own HTTP endpoints are served by Jetty, not Netty; the netty-codec-http module is not present in PingFederate 13.2 at all, and in PingFederate 12.3, 13.0, and 13.1 it is present only as an unused transitive of the AWS SDK's asynchronous Netty transport - PingFederate's AWS integrations (such as DynamoDB) use the SDK's Apache HTTP transport, so the Netty HTTP parser never processes network data. Not exploitable; no change is required.

PingFederate is not affected by CVE-2026-93574. As with CVE-2026-93566, the affected HTTP/1.1 chunked-transfer parser lives in netty-codec-http, which is absent from PingFederate 13.2 and, in 12.3, 13.0, and 13.1, present only as an unused transitive of the AWS SDK's asynchronous Netty transport that PingFederate does not use. The vulnerable parser is never invoked on network data; no change is required.

PingFederate is not affected by CVE-2026-93493. The netty-handler-ssl-ocsp module is not bundled with PingFederate in any supported release; certificate revocation checking (OCSP) is performed by the JDK and Bouncy Castle certificate path validation stacks, not by Netty, so the affected OCSP response validator is never present at runtime. No change is required.

PingFederate is not affected by CVE-2026-93562. The affected Transfer-Encoding validation is in netty-codec-http, which is absent from PingFederate 13.2 and, in 12.3, 13.0, and 13.1, present only as an unused transitive of the AWS SDK's asynchronous Netty transport; PingFederate's HTTP processing is handled by Jetty, and the Netty codec never parses incoming or outgoing HTTP messages. Not exploitable; no change is required.

PingFederate is not affected by CVE-2026-93573. The affected Transfer-Encoding validation is in netty-codec-http, which is absent from PingFederate 13.2 and, in 12.3, 13.0, and 13.1, present only as an unused transitive of the AWS SDK's asynchronous Netty transport that PingFederate does not engage. The vulnerable parser never processes network data; no change is required.

PingFederate is not affected by CVE-2026-93492. The affected HpackEncoder lives in netty-codec-http2, which is absent from PingFederate 13.2 and, in 12.3, 13.0, and 13.1, present only as an unused transitive of the AWS SDK's asynchronous Netty transport; the attack requires an attacker speaking HTTP/2 directly to a Netty endpoint, and PingFederate never operates Netty as an HTTP/2 server or proxy (its HTTP endpoints are Jetty, and its AWS integrations use the Apache transport). Not exploitable; no change is required.

PingFederate is not affected by CVE-2026-93579. The affected HTTP/2 header validation is in netty-codec-http2, which is absent from PingFederate 13.2 and, in 12.3, 13.0, and 13.1, present only as an unused transitive of the AWS SDK's asynchronous Netty transport; the smuggling scenarios require a Netty-based HTTP/2 endpoint translating to HTTP/1.1, a role PingFederate does not run Netty in. Not exploitable; no change is required.

PingFederate is not affected by CVE-2026-93578. The affected code is Netty's OCSP client in the netty-handler-ssl-ocsp module, which is not bundled with PingFederate in any supported release; Netty is never used for certificate status validation, and OCSP inquiries are handled by the JDK and Bouncy Castle stacks. No change is required.

PingFederate bundles Apache WSS4J 1.6.19 and the latest release also ships 1.6.19, both outside the fixed version list, so scanner findings against the bundled jar are expected. The vulnerability resides in WSS4J's DOM security processing engine, which authenticates inbound WS-Security message signatures; PingFederate does not use this engine for any message processing — no WSS4J handler, processor, or signature-validation class is invoked anywhere in the product. PingFederate implements its own WS-Trust STS, and SAML assertion signatures are verified exclusively through PingFederate's own XmlSignatureVerifier, which is built directly on Apache Santuario; the only WSS4J class PingFederate calls is the P_SHA1 key-derivation algorithm for WS-SecureConversation key exchange, which is untouched by this issue. The affected authentication-bypass path is therefore not reachable in PingFederate, and PingFederate will upgrade the bundled library in an upcoming release solely to remediate the scanner finding.

PingFederate is not affected. The bundled WSS4J 1.6.19 is present only as a library dependency, and PingFederate never invokes WSS4J's message-processing pipeline: encrypted SOAP headers are not processed by WSS4J anywhere in the product, and PingFederate's WS-Trust implementation performs its own XML encryption and decryption through Apache Santuario (XMLCipher) and its own signature verification. The EncryptedHeader child-confusion behavior occurs inside WSS4J's header decryption processor, which is unreachable from any PingFederate code path. PingFederate will include the WSS4J upgrade in an upcoming release to clear the scanner finding; there is no exposure to incorrect confidentiality coverage or policy bypass in PingFederate itself.

PingFederate bundles Apache WSS4J 1.6.19, so scanner findings against the bundled jar are expected, but the vulnerable code path is not reachable. The issue lives in WSS4J's processing of attacker-supplied DerivedKeyToken elements in WS-Security message headers, and PingFederate does not use WSS4J's message-processing engine at all — no WSS4J handler, processor, or DerivedKeyToken resolution is invoked anywhere in the product. PingFederate's WS-Trust implementation derives proof keys through WSS4J's P_SHA1 algorithm class only, with the derivation parameters supplied by PingFederate's own KeyProvider, which restricts server-generated key sizes to the AES-128/192/256 set; combined-entropy derivation occurs within PingFederate's own authenticated token-issuance flow, which requires a presenting authentication token before any key derivation takes place. PingFederate will upgrade the bundled WSS4J in an upcoming release to remediate the scanner finding; the unbounded derived-key handling described by this advisory is not exercised by any PingFederate code path.

PingFederate is not affected. The vulnerability resides in WSS4J's DERDecoder, used when WSS4J resolves a signature's key reference through a certificate's SubjectKeyIdentifier extension during WS-Security message processing; PingFederate never invokes WSS4J for signature verification or key-reference resolution. All SAML and XML signature validation in PingFederate — including on the WS-Trust endpoints this class of attack would target — is performed by PingFederate's own XmlSignatureVerifier, built on Apache Santuario (xmlsec 2.2.3-p4), which resolves certificates from X509Data/KeyInfo elements rather than WSS4J's DER decoding path. An attacker cannot steer message processing into the affected WSS4J code, so the oversized-allocation condition is unreachable. PingFederate will include the WSS4J upgrade in an upcoming release to clear the scanner finding.

PingFederate is not affected. The vulnerability resides in WSS4J's UsernameToken nonce replay cache - the component (used by Apache CXF) that remembers previously accepted token nonces and compares them as raw base64 text rather than decoded bytes, allowing a whitespace-padded re-encoding of the same nonce to evade the cache; PingFederate neither bundles Apache CXF nor uses WSS4J's security engine or any nonce replay cache in any release. PingFederate's WS-Trust implementation processes UsernameTokens through its own UsernameTokenProcessor, which validates credentials directly against configured Password Credential Validators and performs no nonce tracking whatsoever — the token model carries the nonce field, but no PingFederate code path stores or compares it, so the base64-canonicalization gap has nothing to bypass. The only WSS4J class PingFederate invokes remains the P_SHA1 key-derivation algorithm, as established in the CVE-2026-88920/85532/95616 dispositions. PingFederate will upgrade the bundled WSS4J in the upcoming release already planned for the other WSS4J findings.

PingFederate is not affected. The vulnerability resides in Bouncy Castle's CMS (Cryptographic Message Syntax / S-MIME) AuthenticatedData parser classes — CMSAuthenticatedDataParser and org.bouncycastle.asn1.cms.AuthenticatedData — and PingFederate does not use Bouncy Castle's CMS API anywhere in the product: there is no CMS, S/MIME, or authenticated-data message processing in any component. PingFederate's bundled Bouncy Castle FIPS libraries are used for JCE crypto primitives, TLS via the BC JSSE provider, OCSP response parsing, and key-derivation — none of which involve the affected parser classes — and we verified no CMS or reviewer class from the affected packages is referenced anywhere in the codebase. The unauthenticated-attribute-injection scenario requires an application that parses attacker-modifiable CMS AuthenticatedData messages, which does not apply to any PingFederate message flow. PingFederate will update the bundled Bouncy Castle libraries in an upcoming release to remediate the scanner finding.

PingFederate is not affected. The vulnerability resides in Bouncy Castle's PKIXCertPathReviewer class, a standalone diagnostic/trust-decision utility; the advisory itself notes that Bouncy Castle's own CertPathValidator ("PKIX", "BC") implementation shares no code with the reviewer and correctly rejects affected chains. PingFederate never references PKIXCertPathReviewer in any release — we verified neither the modern (org.bouncycastle.pkix.jcajce) nor legacy (org.bouncycastle.x509) copy appears in the codebase. PingFederate performs certificate-path validation through its own CertPathValidator.PKIX wrapper (PKIXCertPathValidatorWrapper), which delegates explicitly to the JDK's Sun provider implementation rather than any Bouncy Castle reviewer, and certificate trust decisions in federation connections, TLS, and admin validation all flow through this JDK-backed path. The name-constraint bypass is therefore not reachable, and PingFederate will update the bundled Bouncy Castle libraries in an upcoming release to clear the scanner finding.

PingFederate is not affected. The vulnerability resides in Bouncy Castle's CMS key-transport recipient API (JceKeyTransRecipient with key-size validation enabled), which processes CMS EnvelopedData/AuthEnvelopedData messages using RFC 9709 content-encryption-key derivation — an API surface PingFederate does not use anywhere in the product: no CMS recipient, EnvelopedData, or key-transport processing code exists in any release, and the only key-derivation function PingFederate takes from Bouncy Castle is the X9.63 concatenation KDF used for ECDH key agreement in JWE token decryption, which shares no code with the affected CMS path. PingFederate's own XML encryption operations are performed through Apache Santuario's XMLCipher with explicit AES algorithm selection, not through Bouncy Castle's CMS stack. The silent key-size-validation bypass therefore cannot be triggered through any PingFederate message flow, and PingFederate will update the bundled Bouncy Castle libraries in the same upcoming release already planned for CVE-2026-71888 and CVE-2026-71889.

PingFederate is not meaningfully affected, and not at all for the unauthenticated scenarios this advisory describes. Of the four affected paths, PingFederate uses none of the direct API entry points — no JcePBMac1CalculatorBuilder, no PKCS12PfxPdu/isMacValid PFX parsing, no scrypt, and no OpenSSH private-key parsing anywhere in the product. The only indirect exposure is in Bouncy Castle FIPS mode, where PingFederate's keystore loading can resolve to Bouncy Castle's PKCS12 keystore implementation, whose PBMAC1 handling routes through the unbounded PBKDF2 path — but that code is reachable only when an authenticated administrator deliberately imports or converts a crafted PKCS#12 keystore file, an operation that already grants the actor administrative control of the server, and the standard keystore formats PingFederate processes (JKS, PKCS#12 via the JDK provider in default mode) derive keys through the JDK's own bounded implementation instead. The high-impact case in this advisory — a small untrusted input dictating arbitrary KDF work before any authentication check — has no unauthenticated or low-privilege path into PingFederate. PingFederate will update the bundled Bouncy Castle libraries in the upcoming release already planned for CVE-2026-71888, CVE-2026-71889, and CVE-2026-71892.

PingFederate is not affected. The vulnerable moment version is present in the admin-console frontend — it reaches the shipped JavaScript bundle as a transitive dependency of the UI design-system and timezone libraries — but the exploit requires an application to pass attacker-controlled, non-string input directly to moment.locale(), and no PingFederate code, in any release, calls moment.locale() at all: the only locale() invocations in the shipped bundles are moment's own internal calls, and the application source passes user-supplied data only to sorting and display helpers. The advisory itself scopes the issue primarily to npm server-side users passing user input into locale(), which does not describe any PingFederate component — the affected code executes in the authenticated administrator's browser, not on the server, and the require() call it reaches does not exist in the browser bundle. PingFederate will update the moment library in an upcoming release to clear the scanner finding.

PingFederate's JavaScript toolchain includes the affected brace-expansion library — version 1.1.11 in the 12.3 line and 1.1.18/2.1.4/5.0.9 in the latest release, all below the fixed versions — so scanner findings against the development lockfiles are expected. The library is present only as a transitive build-toolchain dependency (via minimatch under babel, eslint, jest, and glob), confined to the devDependencies used to compile and lint the admin console frontend, and we verified the compiled bundles shipped in the product contain none of its code. The vulnerability requires a crafted glob-style brace pattern to be expanded at runtime, which never occurs in any PingFederate runtime component: patterns are only processed by build tools on the developer's machine against the repository's own build scripts. PingFederate will refresh the build toolchain lockfiles in an upcoming release to resolve the finding; there is no runtime exposure and no attack path from any network-facing component.

PingFederate is not exploitable: the affected library versions present in the build lockfiles (1.1.11 in 12.3; 1.1.18/2.1.4/5.0.9 in the latest release) exist solely in the frontend build toolchain as dev-only transitive dependencies of minimatch, and the code is not present in any JavaScript bundle shipped in the product. The deeply-nested-brace recursion this CVE describes can only be triggered by an untrusted brace pattern supplied to the expand API at runtime, and no PingFederate runtime component — Java server, admin console, or any shipped web asset — invokes brace expansion on user-influenced input. Both brace-expansion CVEs share this disposition; PingFederate will update the affected development dependencies in an upcoming release to clear the scanner finding.

PingFederate is not affected, consistent with the disposition for CVE-2026-102276 and CVE-2026-102278. The affected brace-expansion versions present in the build lockfiles (1.1.11 in the 12.3 line; 1.1.18/2.1.4/5.0.9 in the latest release) exist solely in the frontend build toolchain as dev-only transitive dependencies of minimatch — used by babel, eslint, jest, and glob at build time — and none of the library's code is present in any JavaScript bundle shipped in the product. The vulnerability requires a crafted {a},b}-shaped glob pattern to be supplied to the expand API at runtime, and no PingFederate runtime component — Java server, admin console, or any shipped web asset — performs brace expansion on any input, attacker-influenced or otherwise. Even in the build-toolchain context, the pattern input is the repository's own build scripts, not untrusted data. PingFederate will update the affected development dependencies in the upcoming release already planned for the other brace-expansion findings; there is no runtime exposure and no attack path from any network-facing component.

PingFederate is not affected by CVE-2026-44249. The vulnerable class, IpSubnetFilterRule, is Netty's mechanism for enforcing IP subnet allow/deny rules inside a Netty channel pipeline; PingFederate contains no code that references or installs it, and any IP-based access control PingFederate performs is implemented in its own code and the Jetty servlet container, never in Netty. Although the Netty modules bundled with PingFederate fall within the affected version range, this class is never instantiated, so the faulty IPv6 masking operation is never executed. Not exploitable; no upgrade, mitigation, or configuration change is required.

PingFederate is not affected by CVE-2026-55831. The vulnerable SPDY SETTINGS decoder belongs to the server-side SPDY stack in netty-codec-http, which PingFederate never uses: all PingFederate HTTP endpoints are served by Jetty, no PingFederate code installs Netty handlers into any channel pipeline, and PingFederate does not speak the SPDY protocol to any peer. netty-codec-http is present in PingFederate only as an unused transitive of the AWS SDK's asynchronous transport (and embedded inside the bundled AWS KMS encryptor integration), and it never processes network data. A remote peer cannot open a SPDY session with any PingFederate component, so the amplified SETTINGS allocation cannot occur; not exploitable, and no change is required.

PingFederate is not affected by CVE-2026-55833. The affected SPDY header decompression path lives in netty-codec-http's server-side SPDY stack, which PingFederate never operates: PingFederate's HTTP endpoints are served by Jetty, no PingFederate code installs Netty handlers, and no PingFederate endpoint accepts SPDY connections. netty-codec-http is present in PingFederate 13.1 only as an unused transitive of the AWS SDK's asynchronous transport (and embedded inside the bundled AWS KMS encryptor integration) and never parses network data, so the compression-amplified inflation loop is unreachable. Not exploitable; no upgrade, mitigation, or configuration change is required.

PingFederate is not affected by CVE-2026-56745. The vulnerable SpdyHttpDecoder is a server-side handler that converts SPDY stream frames into HTTP objects and is exercised only when an application explicitly installs Netty's SPDY-to-HTTP codec in a channel pipeline; PingFederate never does so. All PingFederate HTTP processing is performed by Jetty, and the only copies of netty-codec-http in the distribution — the AWS SDK's unused asynchronous-transport transitive and the copy embedded in the AWS KMS encryptor integration — never process network data. No remote peer can send a SYN_STREAM frame to any PingFederate component, so the pooled-buffer leak cannot occur; not exploitable, and no change is required.

PingFederate is not affected by CVE-2026-56819. The vulnerable DelegatingDecompressorFrameListener is part of Netty's HTTP/2 codec, which PingFederate never operates: PingFederate's HTTP/2 endpoints are served by Jetty's HTTP/2 implementation, and no PingFederate code references Netty's HTTP/2 classes. netty-codec-http2 is present in PingFederate 13.1 only as an unused transitive of the AWS SDK's asynchronous transport (and embedded inside the bundled AWS KMS encryptor integration) and never processes network data. The DATA-frame decompression path with the leaking error branch is therefore unreachable by any peer; not exploitable, and no upgrade, mitigation, or configuration change is required.

PingFederate is not affected by CVE-2026-75596. The affected code path is SniHandler, Netty's server-side TLS handler for SNI-based certificate selection, together with its ClientHello aggregation base class SslClientHelloHandler; PingFederate terminates TLS in the Jetty servlet container (or an upstream load balancer) and never in Netty, and a scan of the shipped libraries confirms that neither PingFederate code nor any bundled third-party library references either class. PingFederate's only runtime Netty usage is outbound client connections made by the bundled Redis client library, where SniHandler does not participate. The pre-handshake ClientHello aggregation path is therefore never invoked on any PingFederate endpoint; not exploitable, and no upgrade, mitigation, or configuration change is required.

PingFederate is not affected by CVE-2026-100655. The affected SpdySessionHandler is Netty's SPDY server session handler, and PingFederate never operates Netty as an HTTP or SPDY server: all PingFederate HTTP endpoints are served by Jetty, and no PingFederate code references Netty or installs Netty handlers into any channel pipeline. Netty is present in the distribution only as an unused transitive of the AWS SDK's asynchronous transport, so a remote peer cannot open a SPDY connection to any PingFederate component and the unbounded stream accounting is never exercised. Not exploitable; no upgrade, mitigation, or configuration change is required.

PingFederate is not affected by CVE-2026-100656. The affected code is HttpServerCodec, Netty's HTTP/1.1 server codec: PingFederate's HTTP processing is handled by Jetty, and no PingFederate code references or installs Netty server handlers, so the vulnerable codec is never placed in any channel pipeline and never parses network data. netty-codec-http appears in PingFederate only as an unused transitive of the AWS SDK's asynchronous transport (in 12.3, 13.0, and 13.1; embedded inside the bundled KMS master-key encryptor integration in newer releases), and PingFederate never operates Netty as an HTTP server. The pipelining attack therefore has no reachable target in PingFederate; no upgrade, mitigation, or configuration change is required.

PingFederate is not affected by CVE-2026-100658. The affected WebSocketServerExtensionHandler is only invoked when an application explicitly installs it in a Netty pipeline to negotiate WebSocket extensions, and PingFederate runs no Netty-based HTTP or WebSocket endpoints: its HTTP endpoints are served by Jetty, and no PingFederate code references Netty. The handler is therefore never instantiated, and the HTTP/1.1 pipelining attack cannot reach the unbounded extension queue through any PingFederate component, including through the unused Netty copies shipped inside the AWS KMS master-key encryptor integration. Not exploitable; no upgrade, mitigation, or configuration change is required.

PingFederate is not affected by CVE-2026-109618. This vulnerability resides entirely within the PHP runtime's out-of-memory error handling, and PingFederate is a pure Java application that does not embed, execute, or ship PHP in any form. Because no PHP interpreter or PHP code is present in the product, there is no attack surface for this issue in any supported PingFederate version. No remediation or configuration change is required.

PingFederate is not affected by CVE-2026-109619. This vulnerability is in the PHP runtime's handling of global state across requests, and PingFederate is a pure Java application that does not embed, execute, or ship PHP in any form. Because no PHP interpreter is present in the product, there is no attack surface for this issue in any supported PingFederate version. No remediation or configuration change is required.

Not affected. CVE-2026-111497 is an out-of-bounds write in the Node.js built-in Brotli decoder, exploitable only where a Node.js runtime decompresses attacker-controlled Brotli data. PingFederate does not ship or execute a Node.js runtime: the Node.js-built UI is compiled ahead of time into static JavaScript bundles served by the product, and at request time the browser (not Node.js) renders it and performs any Content-Encoding decompression using the browser's own Brotli implementation, which is separate code and not affected by this CVE. Node.js is used only in CI build containers, which are not deployed to production.

PingFederate is affected by CVE-2026-68497, a denial-of-service flaw in jackson-databind where deserializing an attacker-crafted string into certain XML date/duration types causes excessive CPU consumption. In PingFederate, the reachable path is limited to the SCIM 1.1 API (the meta.created/meta.lastModified fields), which requires valid SCIM credentials and enabled SCIM provisioning - there is no unauthenticated exposure, and the impact is limited to temporary CPU load rather than information disclosure or privilege escalation. PingFederate ships jackson-databind in the affected version range across supported releases, and an upgrade to the fixed version (2.21.6) is already tracked under an existing engineering ticket.

The scan finding against ognl.jar is a false positive, and PingFederate is not affected by CVE-2026-113730. The vulnerability is a bypass of OGNL's stricter-invocation sandbox mode, which does not exist in the OGNL 2.7.3 version shipped with PingFederate — that feature was introduced in the OGNL 3.x line, so there is no sandbox for the bypass technique to defeat. The CVE also requires an application to evaluate attacker-controlled OGNL expressions while relying on that mode as its security sandbox; in PingFederate, OGNL expressions are administrator-authored trusted configuration evaluated against server-side data, protected by application-level controls rather than the library mode. We therefore assess PingFederate as not vulnerable to this CVE, and OGNL will be updated in a regular dependency refresh as defense in depth.

PingFederate uses Jackson polymorphic typing only for server-generated internal state - for example, session records written to and read back from the encrypted session store (encryption enabled by default) - and does not deserialize type identifiers from attacker-supplied JSON. Exploitation of CVE-2026-110879 requires the attacker to control the polymorphic type ID in the JSON being deserialized, which normal PingFederate traffic does not provide. We therefore assess PingFederate as not exploitable through its exposed interfaces; residual risk is limited to scenarios where an attacker can already write to PingFederate's external data store. An updated jackson-databind will be delivered in a regular dependency refresh as defense in depth.

This is a denial-of-service flaw in JSON parsed from character-based input (String/Reader sources), where an excessively long property name is buffered before length limits are enforced; byte-stream JSON parsing - the predominant path in PingFederate - is not affected. A limited number of PingFederate components do parse JSON from character-based input, including some REST endpoints that accept client-submitted JSON, so the affected parsing path is reachable in principle. Practical impact requires an attacker to send many concurrent oversized requests, and standard request-body size limits at a fronting proxy or load balancer constrain the exposure further. We recommend deploying the updated jackson-core in an upcoming release and, as an interim mitigation, enforcing request-body size limits at any reverse proxy in front of PingFederate.

CVE-2026-115876 is currently a reserved CVE ID with no published description; Mend scores it High (7.5) against jackson-dataformat-yaml. PingFederate carries this library only as a transitive dependency, and code review found no PingFederate code path that parses attacker-supplied YAML at runtime. On that basis we assess PingFederate as not vulnerable to this finding, and we will revisit once the CVE description is published. The library will be updated in a regular dependency refresh.

WS-2026-0134 is the SCA vendor's advisory identifier for a jackson-dataformat-yaml issue that does not yet have a published CVE. PingFederate carries this library only as a transitive dependency, and code review found no PingFederate code path that parses attacker-supplied YAML at runtime. On that basis we assess PingFederate as not vulnerable to this advisory. The library will be updated in a regular dependency refresh.

The vulnerable behavior occurs only when Guava collection classes (CompactHashMap, CompactHashSet, MapMakerInternalMap) are deserialized from a crafted Java serialized stream. PingFederate does not deserialize Guava collections from untrusted sources; its Java deserialization paths are confined to authenticated administrative functions operating on server-generated data. We therefore assess PingFederate as not vulnerable to this issue in practice. Guava will be refreshed in an upcoming release as defense in depth.

This CVE describes a denial-of-service issue in Apache Struts 2.0.0 through 2.3.24.1 arising from how Struts caches method references when used with OGNL versions before 3.0.12. PingFederate does not use Apache Struts, and its OGNL usage is limited to administrator-authored mapping expressions as described in our response to CVE-2026-113730. We therefore assess PingFederate as not affected by this CVE. The flagged OGNL version will be refreshed in a regular dependency update, which will also clear this scanner alert.

The affected versions of the auth0 java-jwt library (4.0.0-4.6.1) can terminate a worker thread when parsing a JWT containing an out-of-range exp/nbf/iat timestamp, and this occurs before signature verification; the impact is degraded availability under repeated crafted tokens, with no authentication bypass or information disclosure. A version in the affected range ships with PingFederate for bundled integration components; our code review found no core PingFederate JWT validation paths that use this library. We are updating the bundled library to 4.6.2, which resolves the issue. Exposure in the meantime is limited to denial of service against components that do validate JWTs with this library.

Older maintenance releases of PingFederate are vulnerable to CVE-2026-13505 in all deployment modes. PingFederate uses the Bouncy Castle FIPS provider (bc-fips) for routine cryptographic operations in every mode - XML signature generation and verification, revocation checking, and assertion/token encryption - and additionally routes all TLS through Bouncy Castle in FIPS-mode deployments. Affected bc-fips versions zeroise the sensitive key material held by the AES and DESede engines, the SP 800-90A DRBGs, SymmetricSecretKey, and the PBKD and scrypt parameter classes only from Object.finalize, which runs at an unspecified time on a single finalizer thread. Where PingFederate's traffic allocates these objects faster than that thread retires them - for example, the engine instances created for each signature and encryption operation under sustained load - the pending-finalization queue grows without bound: zeroisation falls arbitrarily far behind, key material stays resident in the heap longer than intended, and the queue growth can contribute to an OutOfMemoryError under load. The impact is primarily availability; PingFederate runs on Java 17, one of the later JVMs on which this behavior is most pronounced. We have updated the bc-fips library to version 2.1.3, the first fixed release in the 2.1.X series, in all maintenance releases, which resolves this issue.

Older maintenance releases of PingFederate are vulnerable. PF parses attacker-influenced ASN.1 with BC directly in all deployment modes - OCSPCheckerImpl uses org.bouncycastle.asn1.ASN1InputStream to process OCSP responses fetched over the network, and OCSPReq/BasicOCSPResp/X509CertificateHolder all sit on the lazy ASN.1 layer. In FIPS mode, all certificate decoding (including client certs presented during TLS handshakes) also routes through BC's ASN.1 parser. A deeply nested lazily-parsed sequence that resets the nesting-depth guard could cause a stack-overflow DoS from network-supplied input. We have updated the bc-fips library to version 2.1.3, the first fixed release in the 2.1.X series, in all maintenance releases, which resolves this issue.

Older maintenance releases of PingFederate are vulnerable to CVE-2026-8763 only in FIPS-mode deployments. In FIPS mode, the Bouncy Castle FIPS provider (bc-fips) performs PKIX certificate path validation for PingFederate's certificate trust decisions (certificate authentication, WS-Trust, and XML signature verification), and affected versions allow a name-constrained intermediate CA to bypass rfc822Name and URI name constraints by issuing a certificate with a trailing-dot name in the Subject Alternative Name. Exploitation requires a trusted, name-constrained CA in the deployment; non-FIPS deployments use the JDK's certificate path validation and are not affected. We have updated the bc-fips library to version 2.1.3, the first fixed release in the 2.1.X series, in all maintenance releases, which resolves this issue.

PingFederate is not affected by CVE-2026-47884. This issue arises when a Spring MVC application renders XsltView through an implicit "/**" mapping, and PingFederate neither uses Spring MVC nor the XsltView class anywhere in its codebase - its server-side web layer is Jetty, Jersey, and Tapestry, with the React admin console as a browser-side static application. The bundled Spring Framework 6.2.19 libraries are used solely as an internal dependency-injection container. No update or configuration change is required.

PingFederate is not affected by CVE-2026-47887. The vulnerability requires the application to map Spring's UrlFileNameViewController with an end-of-path mapping and no configured prefix, and that class is not used anywhere in PingFederate - the product does not use Spring MVC request handling on the server side, and its React admin console is a browser-side application served as static assets. The bundled Spring Framework 6.2.19 libraries are used solely as an internal dependency-injection container. No update or configuration change is required.

PingFederate is not affected by CVE-2026-47890. This issue arises when a Spring MVC application uses Server-Sent Events (SSE) together with view fragments, and PingFederate does not use Spring MVC or SSE in any form - its server-side web layer is built on Jetty, Jersey, and Tapestry, while its React admin console is a browser-side application served as static assets and does not involve Spring. The bundled Spring Framework 6.2.19 libraries are used solely as an internal dependency-injection container, so no vulnerable code path exists. No update or configuration change is required.

PingFederate is not affected by CVE-2026-47892. This issue affects WebFlux applications using functional endpoints and deployed with DispatcherServlet - neither WebFlux nor DispatcherServlet is present in PingFederate, which uses Jetty, Jersey, and Tapestry for server-side request handling, with the React admin console as a browser-side static application. The bundled Spring Framework 6.2.19 libraries never process HTTP requests. No update or configuration change is required.

PingFederate is not affected by CVE-2026-47893. The vulnerability requires a Spring WebFlux application that supports WebSocket connections, and PingFederate uses neither Spring WebFlux nor Spring WebSocket support - its server-side web layer is Jetty, Jersey, and Tapestry, with the React admin console as a browser-side application. The bundled Spring Framework 6.2.19 libraries serve only as an internal dependency-injection container, so the vulnerable exception-handling path is never reached. No update or configuration change is required.

PingFederate is not affected by this vulnerability on the releases in question. The flaw is resolved in bc-fips 2.1.3, the first fixed release in the 2.1.x series of the Bouncy Castle FIPS provider, and PingFederate 13.1.3 and later ship exactly that version. The vulnerable code path is PKCS#12 keystore processing, which PingFederate performs only on administrator-configured keystore files, not on attacker-supplied input. Customers on older maintenance releases that bundle bc-fips 2.0.x should upgrade to 12.3.9, 13.1.3, or later.

PingFederate is not affected by this vulnerability on the releases in question. The flaw is in Bouncy Castle's ASN.1 definite-length parsing and is fixed in bc-fips 2.1.3, which PingFederate 13.1.3 and later ship. ASN.1 data that PingFederate parses from network sources (OCSP responses, certificates) is therefore processed by a library version containing the fix. Customers on older maintenance releases bundling bc-fips 2.0.x should upgrade to 12.3.9, 13.1.3, or later.

PingFederate is not affected by this vulnerability on the releases in question. The flaw is fixed in bc-fips 2.1.3, which PingFederate 13.1.3 and later ship, and PingFederate does stringify certificate subject and issuer names from network-presented certificates, so the version fix is the relevant protection. Certificates presented to PingFederate are also generally validated through TLS handshakes or administrative configuration, which limits the volume and rate of parsing. Customers on older maintenance releases bundling bc-fips 2.0.x should upgrade to 12.3.9, 13.1.3, or later.

PingFederate is not affected by this vulnerability on the releases in question. The flaw is fixed in bc-fips 2.1.3, which PingFederate 13.1.3 and later ship. In addition, PingFederate does not use the HSS/LMS post-quantum signature algorithms this flaw is reached through in any supported configuration, so there is no processing path for it regardless. Customers on older maintenance releases bundling bc-fips 2.0.x should upgrade to 12.3.9, 13.1.3, or later.

PingFederate is not affected by this vulnerability on the releases in question. The flaw is fixed in bc-fips 2.1.3, which PingFederate 13.1.3 and later ship for all cryptographic operations, including token and assertion encryption. Customers on older maintenance releases bundling bc-fips 2.0.x should upgrade to 12.3.9, 13.1.3, or later.

PingFederate is not affected by this vulnerability on the releases in question. The flaw is fixed in bc-fips 2.1.3, which PingFederate 13.1.3 and later ship, and PingFederate's revocation checking binds OCSP responses to the certificate being validated. Customers on older maintenance releases bundling bc-fips 2.0.x should upgrade to 12.3.9, 13.1.3, or later.

PingFederate is not affected by this vulnerability on the releases in question. The flaw is fixed in bc-fips 2.1.3, which PingFederate 13.1.3 and later ship. The vulnerable code path is BCFKS keystore loading, which in PingFederate operates on administrator-configured local files rather than network-supplied data, providing additional separation from attacker control. Customers on older maintenance releases bundling bc-fips 2.0.x should upgrade to 12.3.9, 13.1.3, or later.

PingFederate is not affected by this vulnerability on the releases in question. The affected range for the Bouncy Castle FIPS provider is 2.1.0 before 2.1.3, and PingFederate 13.1.3 and later ship bc-fips 2.1.3, which contains the fix. Customers on releases bundling bc-fips 2.0.x are outside the stated affected range for this particular CVE but should still move to 12.3.9, 13.1.3, or later to pick up the other Bouncy Castle fixes described above.

PingFederate is not affected by this vulnerability on the releases in question. The flaw is in the bctls-fips TLS library and is fixed in bctls-fips 2.1.24, the first fixed release in the 2.1.x series, which PingFederate 13.1.3 and later ship. PingFederate 13.1.3 and the current mainline ship jackson-core 2.21.1, which predates the completed fix for this advisory on the 2.21.x line (2.21.2 or later). The impact is limited to denial-of-service hardening: an oversized JSON document may bypass the configured document-length limit in some parser entry points, and exploiting it requires an attacker to deliver very large JSON bodies to an endpoint that parses them, with standard fronting-proxy body-size limits further constraining exposure. As an interim mitigation, we recommend enforcing request-body size limits at any reverse proxy in front of PingFederate.
